name: Mid-century modern

influenced_by: Bauhaus emigres teaching in the US
postwar suburban housing boom and new manufacturing materials (molded plywood, fiberglass)

places: Palm Springs, California; Scandinavia (parallel, related development)
garments: not a fashion look — furniture and architecture (the term itself was coined retrospectively by design historian Cara Greenberg, 1984)

media.title: Charles and Ray Eames's molded plywood and fiberglass chairs (late 1940s–50s)

reacts_against: prewar formality and ornament, favoring clean lines, new industrial materials and an optimistic, functional domestic modernism suited to postwar suburban life.
revivals: a sustained, never-really-left design market; Palm Springs holds an annual Modernism Week

wiki_facts.key_motifs: Clean lines, organic and geometric forms, functionality over ornament, open-plan spaces, large windows, integration with nature
wiki_facts.key_colours: Earthy tones (wood, greens, browns) mixed with pops of bold color (mustard yellow, orange, turquoise)
wiki_facts.key_values: Simplicity, functionality, optimism, modernity, connection to nature

findings: mostly muted — about 64% of the measured color is low-saturation (greys, dusty tones)
measured.caveat: Colors measured from the Aesthetics Wiki images as photographed and displayed on screen; actual materials vary, and screen colors are approximate.
